app_summary: A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs. Supported Operations: Create text post (optional media: image, video, shortened URL, user tag), Read post, Read entire user timeline, Receive recommendations on which users to follow, Search database for user or post, Register/Login using user credentials, Follow/Unfollow user

rca_analyses_list.diagnosis: The url-shorten MongoDB pod fails on startup because TLS is required in its mongod.conf but the TLS certificate provided via the mongodb-tls secret is invalid (expired). Concrete evidence: mongod log: "The provided SSL certificate is expired or not yet valid." followed by a fatal assertion and abort; container terminated with Exit Code 14 and entered CrashLoopBackOff. The ConfigMap-mounted mongod.conf sets net.tls.mode: requireTLS and certificateKeyFile: /etc/tls/tls.pem, so mongod refuses to start with the expired cert.

args.investigation_summary: I inspected cluster pods and found one MongoDB pod in CrashLoopBackOff (url-shorten-mongodb-766c578c7d-hgv9z). evaluation.rca_motivation: Both focus on the url-shorten MongoDB and TLS, but the ground truth says the outage is due to a newly enforced requireTLS breaking the client connection, while the agent incorrectly claims MongoDB itself fails to start because of an expired certificate. The component is roughly right (MongoDB for url-shortener) but the mechanical root cause is different and contradicts the actual scenario.
